finding.claim: The unauthenticated GET /rss endpoint passes the query parameter `u` straight to URI.open. Any visitor can make the server fetch an arbitrary http, https or ftp URL, including internal hosts, loopback and cloud metadata endpoints. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller, so the SSRF is non-blind and leaks data.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open and fetched, following redirects
The first 400 bytes of the response body are returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, or DNS pinning. open-uri follows redirects, though it blocks https-to-http downgrades. No authentication or middleware on the route. The TRUSTED allowlist is applied only on /trusted, not here.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes attacker-controlled params[:u] directly to URI.open with no auth, allowlist or IP filtering (the TRUSTED check exists only at app.rb:14 on /trusted), and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes to the caller.
